correctness.rationale: Exact grounded wheel inverse K_a^{-1} is checked against its recurrence; positivity, reflection symmetry and strict cyclic convexity of its entries fix every absolute-value sign. Spoke rows equal 1+2sqrt(a)(g0-gm); rim rows equal 2sqrt(a)(g0-gm)+4(g0-g1), with the Green source equation giving 2-2ag0+2sqrt(a)(g0-gm). Both edge orbits are exhaustive; a signed edge input realizes each row sum. The strict positive derivative of a e_0^TK_a^{-1}e_0 proves the unique transition. Geometric decay and constant-mode spectral splitting prove both order-of-limits statements. Standard-library exact inversion independently confirms 78 graph/conductance profiles, operator symmetry/trace and selected idempotence, not universal infinity proofs. Endpoints a>0 are observed and limiting a=0 is never treated as an actual included conductance.

originality.rationale: Bapat–Gupta already determines the weighted-wheel Green kernel and individual resistances; no priority is claimed for those. Its fully readable wheel theorems do not state the sharp absolute transfer-current edge row sums, their crossover or singular network-size behavior. General electrical routing estimates and the separately read wheel ellipsoid work have different targets. The accessible historical wheel and electrical-projector records describe distinct invariants or graph classes. Distinct implication comparisons and the source-inspection limitations are given below; earlier equivalent electrical-circuit calculations remain possible.
residual_risks: The complete pairwise-resistance matrix for weighted wheels is known, and someone may have already summed its implied transfer-current absolute values without using the terminology searched.
The older circuit literature is broad; bibliographic search and available original texts cannot prove worldwide uniqueness.
The first-public-date field uses verified arXiv 2009-09-15; the Bapat–Gupta manuscript displays an earlier author date, but this is not evidence of an earlier public release.

value.rationale: For a natural planar network family with overlapping cycles and two symmetry classes of conductance-weighted edges, the exact maximum norm quantifies sharp worst-case edge-signal sensitivity. The two-row formula yields a unique physically meaningful switching conductance a_n whose location is classified in every graph size and tends to 4/3, and the sharp bounded-versus-vanishing-spoke limit noncommutation (3 versus 2) identifies a meaningful finite-size singularity. These exact structural and asymptotic features go beyond listing elementary sample values; they motivate robustness comparisons between hub and rim perturbations.
